principles: A vessel appearing in one AIS snapshot is not automatically classified as new.
A vessel missing from one AIS snapshot is treated as temporarily missing.
Zone changes require consecutive observations of the same vessel.
Confirmed Hormuz transit requires an observed three-zone path through the strait.
Direct Persian Gulf to Gulf of Oman jumps are possible skipped-zone transits, not confirmed transits.
AIS absence is not evidence of physical vessel absence.
AIS suppression, GPS jamming, dark transit and coverage gaps may affect observations.
DWT and vessel counts are logistics indicators, not direct physical oil throughput.

data_quality.interpretation: Quality measures usability of the AIS vessel observation and persistent tracking layer. It does not measure physical oil-flow accuracy.

integration.reason: Persistent tracking is now enabled, but several sequential runs are required to validate confirmed transit detection.
integration.next_step: Collect sequential snapshots and validate confirmed Hormuz transit events.
